items.en: Who are called infants?
items.hint: a noun with adjective in the nominative and a relative clause
choices: līberī nautārum quī patrēs nōn vident

items.en: Where does a little infant usually lie?
items.hint: ablative after 'in' (place where)

items.en: On what does a toothless infant live?
items.hint: a noun in the ablative (lives on ...)

items.q: Ā quā īnfans alitur, sī māter ipsa eum alere nōn potest?
items.en: By whom is the infant fed, if the mother herself cannot feed it?
items.hint: ablative after 'ab' (by another ...)

items.q: Ā quibus multī īnfantēs Rōmānī aluntur?
items.en: By whom are many Roman infants fed?
items.hint: ablative after 'ā' (by whom)

items.en: What are the cradle like now?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative plural

items.en: When will a new baby be born?
items.hint: accusative after 'post' (after ...)

items.q: Quot līberōs tum Iūlius et Aemilia habēbunt?
items.en: How many children will Julius and Aemilia have then?
items.hint: a number with 'līberōs' in the accusative

items.en: What will Aemilia be called by the baby?
items.hint: a name in the nominative (after a passive verb)

items.q: Cūr īnfans 'mamma' et 'tata' dīcet, nōn 'māter' et 'pater'?
items.en: Why will the baby say 'mamma' and 'tata', not 'māter' and 'pater'?
answers: quia ea nōmina dīcere nōn poterit
items.hint: a reason with the future of 'posse' (it will not be able to ...)

items.q: Quis initiō īnfantem sustinēbit ac manū dūcet?
items.en: Who will hold the baby up and lead it by the hand at first?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.en: By whom will the walking baby be praised?
items.hint: ablative after 'ā' (by whom)

items.q: Utra īnfantem alet, māterne an nūtrīx?
items.en: Which of the two will feed Aemilia's baby, the mother or the nurse?
items.hint: a noun in the ablative after 'ā' (by whom, in the passive sentence)

items.en: Where will the maids carry the cradle to in the evening?
items.hint: accusative after 'in' (motion into)

items.en: In what state does Aemilia sit down in the chair?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative (agreeing with Aemilia)

items.q: Dē quō tempore marītus et uxor iam colloquuntur?
items.en: About what time are husband and wife now talking?
items.hint: ablative after 'dē' (about ...)

items.en: What does Julius now understand?
items.hint: an accusative with infinitive (that Aemilia ...)

items.en: What does Aemilia want to have?
items.hint: a noun with adjective in the accusative (the object)

items.q: Quem Iūlius magis amābit quam parvulam fīliam?
items.en: Whom will Julius love more than a little daughter?
items.hint: a pronoun in the accusative (nobody)

items.en: Whom does Julius often praise?
items.hint: two names in the accusative (the objects)

items.en: What kind of girl is Julia?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative

items.en: Towards what does Aemilia take a step?
items.hint: accusative after 'adversus' (towards ...)

items.en: Does Aemilia go away?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (she stays)

items.q: Nōnne Aemilia apud īnfantem suum manēbit?
items.en: Won't Aemilia stay with her baby?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'nōnne' expects 'yes'

items.en: What is a mother's duty?
items.hint: two infinitives (to ... and to ...)

items.en: When will Aemilia be with the baby?
items.hint: ablative of time (by day and by ...)

items.q: Quid est officium Iūliī, ut ipse dīcit?

items.hint: two infinitives (to ... and to ...)

items.en: For whom is sleep necessary?
items.hint: a noun in the dative (necessary for ...)

items.en: Who meets the mistress in the doorway?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.q: Cūr Syra et Iūlia in hortō nōn manent?
items.en: Why don't Syra and Julia stay in the garden?
items.hint: a reason with 'quia' and a future verb (rain is coming)

items.en: What will those clouds bring?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.en: Where does Julius go into?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (motion into)

items.q: Quid Iūlius et Aemilia in ātriō aspiciunt?
items.en: What do Julius and Aemilia watch in the atrium?
items.hint: accusative noun with a present participle

items.en: Why is Julia glad?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' (her father is not ...)

items.en: When will Julius go to Rome?
items.hint: an adverb of time

items.q: Num Iūlius in terrās aliēnās ībit, ut nauta?
items.en: Will Julius go to foreign lands, like a sailor?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no'

items.en: When will Julia go to meet her father?
items.hint: an adverb of time (every ...)

items.en: Does Julia have a sister?

items.en: Why doesn't Julia want a sister?
answers: quia soror sōla amābitur, ipsa nōn amābitur
items.hint: a reason with future passive verbs (the sister alone will be ...)

items.en: When will Julia be happy?
items.hint: a 'sī' clause with a future passive verb

items.q: Quī ita loquuntur, ut Aemilia dīcit?
items.en: Who talk like that, according to Aemilia?
items.hint: a noun with adjective in the nominative plural

items.en: What will Julia be called by her parents?
items.hint: a name in the nominative (after a passive verb)
